chunks: From him, from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Hariz, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said:

I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) about a Muslim who slaughtered a sheep, recited the name [of God], but his knife slipped and exposed the head [of the sheep], so he said: 'If the blood has flowed, eat [it].'
ai.seo_question: Is an animal halal if the knife slips and exposes the head during slaughter?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) clarifies the validity of slaughter when the knife slips and severs the head, a scenario often debated regarding the completeness of the cut. The Imam’s condition that the meat is permissible provided blood has flowed emphasizes the Shia jurisprudential focus on the actual effusion of blood as a sign of life cessation, rather than a rigid requirement for a specific number of cuts. This ruling underscores the practical flexibility in the mechanics of dhabihah as long as the essential conditions of naming Allah and blood flow are met.
